llm.summary: The dominant new fact is Microsoft's Maia 300: the largest single buyer of AI silicon just told the market it intends to run more of its fleet on homegrown chips, and Intel's and Broadcom's CEOs simultaneously warned that capital — not chips, not power — is becoming AI's binding constraint. That is a two-sided message: the demand for compute is real enough that Nvidia has reportedly stopped making RTX 5090 consumer cards to free capacity for RTX Pro data-centre parts, and SpaceX is seeking $40bn of debt to buy Nvidia silicon, but the funding stack is visibly straining after the Firmus shelving and the $30bn Australian data-centre IPO debacle. Macro has re-tightened versus yesterday's reprieve: the dollar is near an 18-month high, crude is back above $100, Treasury yields are elevated, mortgage rates are near 7.5% with credible forecasts of 8%, and the live debate is whether the Fed holds off a rate HIKE — with CPI, PPI and a Warsh speech all this week. The regime file confirms the rotation: Goldilocks and Contraction both falling, Reflation and Stagflation both rising ~5 points. Flows are a one-sector market again — Technology +63, Energy +48, everything else negative, Real Estate -85 and Utilities -71 — with small-cap flows negative and growth beating value by 77 points. The consumer is bifurcating hard: Walmart and TJX raised guidance and Costco sales ran +13% while Wendy's withdrew 2026 guidance and cut its dividend, and pawnbroker Ramsdens doubled gold profits because people are selling jewellery for cash. For the book, the actionable item is HPQ gapping -6.9% pre-market — the most likely cause is AI-driven memory cost inflation crushing PC OEM gross margins, which attacks the exact 'margins/FCF improving' leg of the thesis — alongside SMCI's officer-change 8-K now compounded by a contractor pleading guilty to smuggling $2.5bn of Nvidia servers to China.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: a tightening tape masquerading as a narrow bull market. The three-factor relief of last week has reversed — dollar at an 18-month high, Brent back above $100, long yields elevated — and the Fed conversation is about whether to skip a hike, not deliver a cut. That is mechanically hostile to everything except megacap Technology and Energy, which is exactly what flows show (+63 and +48 against Real Estate -85, Utilities -71, Financials -68). Wednesday's CPI is the single pivot: a hot print with oil over $100 validates the Stagflation branch that just gained 5.2 points, re-prices small caps (already in their worst losing streak in years) and pushes mortgages toward 8%. Bitcoin stuck at $83k while gold holds $4,100-4,200 tells you this is a real-rate and dollar problem, not a liquidity flood — gold is the debasement hedge that works, crypto is trading as a high-beta liquidity asset and failing. Trade dispersion, not direction: toll-takers with contracted backlogs and the custom-silicon supply chain (AVGO, MRVL, TSMC, ASML, LRCX) hold; anything requiring primary capital, consumer credit, or a 30-year mortgage degrades regardless of the index.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the AI trade bifurcates between merchant GPU and custom silicon, and between operators funded by cash flow versus credit. Maia 300 plus AMD-backed MangoBoost plus Naver/FPT GPUaaS says the hyperscalers are systematically attacking the one line item that most determines their margin — Nvidia's take rate on inference. Nvidia keeps the training frontier and is cannibalising its own gaming business to serve it, but the incremental dollar of 2027 inference capex increasingly goes to ASICs, networking and foundry, which is why ASML and TSMC earnings this week matter more than any single model release. Meanwhile the Intel/Broadcom capital-crunch warning is the real signal: with the dollar at 18-month highs and term premium structural, the marginal neocloud, SPV and GPU-collateralised deal does not clear, so consolidation and vendor financing increase and credit quality within the AI complex becomes the dominant factor. Physical demand stays underwritten — ERCOT load through the 2030s, PJM restarting its interconnection queue, Philippines and Czech nuclear, Russia building four reactors in Iran — while Utilities sit in the most-hated flow bucket at -71 against CEG attention 94/pricing 55 and VST 90/47. That gap closes in favour of electrons. Macro stays sticky-inflation with a reflation tilt: oil over $100, Hormuz risk to Asian LNG, Gulf shut-ins at 57.5%, tariff pass-through, and a Fed whose chair is now Warsh.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: first, compute and generation are a single capital decision, and the scarce assets are firm power, cooling, grid equipment and residual-value-bearing silicon — not models. Second, the hyperscaler-designed chip is the structural story of this decade: vertical integration will compress merchant semiconductor rents the way private label compressed branded CPG, and the durable winners are the design partners and the tool/foundry layer that get paid regardless of whose logo is on the die. Third, the cost of capital has permanently reset higher — mortgages above 7% through 2027, housing chronically undersupplied because existing owners are locked in and builders cannot clear at 8%, which keeps rents and shelter inflation structurally elevated and keeps the consumer bifurcated between asset owners and wage earners. That bifurcation is already visible: Walmart, TJX and Costco gaining share while mid-market restaurants withdraw guidance. Fourth, gold at $4,100+ with record central-bank buying while Bitcoin stalls at $83k suggests sovereign debasement hedging is being expressed through official-sector metal, not retail crypto, and that distinction will persist.

short_term: Trading down is now the base case, not a tail: Costco sales +13%, Walmart and TJX both raising guidance, while Wendy's withdraws 2026 guidance and cuts its dividend — consumers are shifting spend from discretionary occasions to bulk value and off-price.

Households are liquidating stored value for liquidity: Ramsdens' gold-buying profits doubled, which is the behaviour of people monetising jewellery at $4,100 gold because cash flow is tight, not of people accumulating hard assets.

Housing demand is being met by staying put: at 7.5% mortgages trending toward 8%, Americans are souring on the economy specifically through the housing channel, suppressing moving-linked spend (furniture, appliances, Home Depot/Target basket).

Investors are crowding one sector: Technology flows +63 against negative everything else, growth beating value by 77 points, family offices chasing AI on FOMO per survey — attention and capital are concentrating exactly as the funding window for second-tier AI narrows.

Retail curiosity is migrating to stablecoins (Digital Payments attention 80, +33.5%) and Starlink (Space 67, +38.3%) — people are shopping for dollar-substitutes and for connectivity that bypasses incumbent carriers.
Enterprises are cutting people to fund technology: Visa booked $563m of job-cut costs against resilient spending volumes — the pattern of using AI-era budgets to shrink headcount rather than grow it.

Electricity has become a consumer anxiety line item — rising searches skew to 'electricity bill assistance' and 'bill payment', meaning data-centre load growth is being felt as a household bill before it is felt as a utility earnings beat.
long_term: Security and sovereignty over convenience: the Philippines adding nuclear to attract data centres, Türkiye sizing wind against $4bn of gas imports, India shielding city-gas users from a Hormuz shock — nations are buying energy independence at a price premium, permanently.

Knowledge and productivity work shifts from headcount to agent fleets, which converts a labour cost into a compute-and-power cost — and therefore into an electricity, cooling and silicon demand curve that does not mean-revert with the business cycle.

Status consumption is splitting: luxury proxies like Laopu Gold see target cuts on consumer pressure while value retail compounds share — the middle of the consumption distribution keeps hollowing out.
Mobility and connectivity de-couple from terrestrial incumbents as satellite direct-to-device scales, eroding the rent incumbent carriers and cable collect on geography.

Healthspan becomes a purchased good rather than a medical event — continuous glucose monitoring, longevity supplements and metabolic management move from patient populations to consumer populations, which is the structural tailwind under DXCM.

Capital formation moves private: when a $5bn and a $30bn data-centre listing both fail, infrastructure of this scale gets funded by sovereigns, private credit and corporate balance sheets, and public equity investors get a lower share of the build's economics.

portfolio_implications.why: Pre-market gap -6.9% is the single biggest portfolio event today and there is no benign explanation in the tape. The most probable driver is AI-driven memory cost inflation compressing PC gross margins — the same force that makes MU a winner makes HPQ a structural loser. That directly contradicts the 'FCF improving, valuation below sector peers' rationale: a cheap multiple on a margin that is about to be transferred to Micron is not cheap. Establish the cause before the open; if it is memory cost or a guidance cut, this is a thesis break, not a dip.

At a 5% weight this is the most headline-fragile position in the book. The 10/08 officer-change 8-K is now compounded by a contractor pleading guilty to smuggling $2.5bn of Nvidia AI servers to China — governance and export-control risk at a company whose entire bull case rests on being trusted with allocation of scarce silicon. The DigiPowerX Blackwell win confirms demand is real, so this is a position-sizing decision, not an exit: cut to a size where a compliance headline is survivable.

Software sits third in the flow ranking behind Cybersecurity and Cloud, and Palantir printing 93% revenue growth with a 155% Rule of 40 resets the bar for what 'AI-exposed software' means. CRM's case is FCF and a depressed multiple, not growth — that works in a flat tape but will not lead. Hold the weight, do not add until there is evidence agent revenue is additive rather than seat-cannibalising.

Industrials flows at -57 and a value-retail cohort that is winning on price, not on store capex, means the automation order cycle is not accelerating here yet. The AI-native factory announcements (LTTS/NVIDIA, Hyundai Steel) are the right long-term direction but none of today's capital is flowing to it. Hold; this is a two-to-three-quarter patience trade.

The cleanest defensive growth in the book against a stagflationary setup: $100 crude and 7.5% mortgages do not change a diabetic's sensor replacement schedule. Margins, ROIC and FCF all expanding, longevity attention rising, Health Care flows only -10 versus Real Estate -85 and Utilities -71. If HPQ is reduced, this is the natural recipient of the capital.

Revenue accelerating with valuation below both its own history and sector peers makes it the correct ballast if CPI runs hot on Wednesday and the Reflation/Stagflation branch (now 46% combined and rising) dominates. No catalyst today; hold and let it do its job as the non-correlated sleeve.

The book is six names at 5% each — roughly 70% uncommitted. With the dollar at an 18-month high, crude above $100, a live Fed hike debate, CPI and PPI this week, and bank earnings beginning, there is no premium for being early. Keep the dry powder for a post-CPI dislocation in the power complex (CEG/VST/EQT, where attention-versus-pricing gaps are widest) rather than deploying into an index that is already concentrated in one sector.
